question: Should a component be separated from its gate, so the component becomes a reusable tool and the gate becomes an independently inspectable thing? Akien opened the 2026-08-12 design conversation with exactly this — with orientation as the worked example — and the conversation resolved the TAXONOMY (tools/machines/devices/instances) without ever returning to the proposal that prompted it. Undecided, and it is the half with code consequences.
whats_beyond: The pattern already exists three times and has a name: a SIEVE is the reusable tool, a MESH is that sieve bound to one chokepoint at one owner's address (inference_domain owns the host mesh, db_domain the 5432 mesh). So this is finishing a migration rather than inventing one. THE ARGUMENT FOR IT IS NOT THE ONE AKIEN LED WITH: he offered reusability and waved off inspectors as 'not a problem, we should have that anyway' — but you CANNOT PUT AN INSPECTOR ON A GATE THAT LIVES INSIDE A FUNCTION BODY, and chart's orient gate is exactly that today (write_packet, judges called inline). Nothing can watch it, so nothing can learn it. Gate-separation is therefore the precondition for learns-its-gates, a founding intention — which is a stronger trace than reuse. Beyond here: whether every gate separates or only some; what a separated gate costs at the call sites that fire inline today; and whether an inspector-per-gate is one class instantiated many times (his 2026-08-11 reading: 'it should be a class, and we should instantiate a gate and an inspector for each gate') or something per-gate. Kin: the /reorient intent (berth intent-20260811T212743-968fbdc07e59) measured that chart's orient is held on the build rail by GATING rather than capability — the same weld, from the other end.
source: Akien's opening turn, 2026-08-12: 'perhaps we need to redesign the components so that they are seperate from their gates to render them reusable? ... the idea is the learning component that is orientation would become it's own TOOL, just as we did with mesh/nest/seive.' Recorded verbatim in decisions/2026-08-12-tools-machines-devices-instances.json, which settles the taxonomy and explicitly does not settle this.
